coverage_notes.prior_check: The immediately preceding hourly recall check completed its search but its heartbeat write failed; this run uses that prior check's approximate completion boundary as the start of the search window.

primary_checks.result: Checked first via current OCHA OPT homepage and targeted search. Checked second via WHO's current conflict page and targeted search. No new in-window Gaza health-system, hospital, ambulance, fuel, medical-evacuation, or functioning-capacity development was established.

degraded_reasons: The targeted UN News search was blocked by robots.txt. Other humanitarian, primary-source, Reuters, AP, UNRWA, WFP, MSF, crossing, casualty, infrastructure, and ceasefire searches remained usable.
notable_exclusions: Reuters' 7 October anniversary report was published at 05:03 UTC on 7 October (22:03 PDT on 6 October), before this search window, and was contextual rather than a new in-window Gaza development.
Reuters' report of two Palestinians killed in Gaza City was published 6 October at 10:12 UTC and was already known from earlier watches.
AP's rolling Middle East report repeated two Gaza City deaths on Tuesday, matching the already-known 6 October casualty event rather than establishing a new event after the prior check.
AP's 7 October satellite-demolition feature was retrospective, with evidence through September and 6 October, and did not establish a new operational change within this watch window.
WAFA-targeted results surfaced no newer qualifying Gaza event than 2 October.
Background, retrospective, duplicate, unsupported, and pre-window items were excluded.
coverage_notes.conclusion: No new traceable qualifying development was established since the prior hourly check; useful coverage remained despite one blocked source.
